sections.heading: Core Gameplay Mechanics
sections.body:
At its core, Toddler Tile Image Scramble is a puzzle game that requires players to match and arrange tiles to reveal a hidden image. 
      The game's core mechanics are simple yet engaging, making it accessible to a wide range of players. 
      Players are presented with a grid of tiles, each featuring a different image. 
      The goal is to slide the tiles around until the images match, forming a complete picture.

The game's grid is divided into rows and columns, each containing a set of tiles. 
Players can move tiles horizontally or vertically, but not diagonally. 
When a player moves a tile, the adjacent tiles are automatically rearranged to make space. 
This mechanic adds a fun twist to the game, requiring players to think strategically about how to move the tiles to create a matching pair.

One of the game's unique features is its use of randomization. 
Each time a player starts a new game, the tiles are shuffled, presenting a new puzzle to solve. 
This ensures that the game remains challenging and engaging, even after playing multiple times. 
The randomization also makes it difficult to memorize the location of specific tiles, adding an extra layer of complexity to the gameplay.

Overall, the game's core mechanics are well-designed and engaging, making it a joy to play. 
The simplicity and addictiveness of the game's mechanics make it an excellent choice for players of all ages, from young children to adults.
